recipes.name: Lemon-oregano chicken with blistered pepper rice
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it with the water amount on its package. Keep covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Cut chicken into 2 cm pieces. Toss with half the oil, minced garlic, oregano, salt and half the lemon juice. Keep raw chicken separate from the vegetables.
Heat a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add the remaining oil and sliced peppers; cook 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned at the edges. Transfer to a plate.
Add chicken in one layer. Cook for 8–12 minutes, turning as it browns, until the thickest pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Add a splash of water if the pan dries out.

Add turkey, garlic, smoked paprika, cumin and salt. Break the turkey into small pieces and cook 8–10 minutes until it reaches 165°F / 74°C.

Mix miso, finely grated ginger and garlic, maple syrup, lime juice and 15 ml water. Pat the salmon dry and spread the mixture over its top.

Move broccoli to the sides and place salmon on the tray. Roast for about 10–15 minutes more, checking the thickest part of the fish reaches 145°F / 63°C. Remove fish when ready; leave broccoli longer if needed.

Mix harissa, oil, grated garlic, cumin, salt and half the lemon juice. Toss with tofu, chickpeas and sliced peppers.
Spread in a single layer on a lined tray. Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until peppers soften and tofu edges brown.
Meanwhile rinse quinoa and cook according to the package. Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff and stir in the remaining lemon juice.
Divide quinoa and the tray mixture into three portions. Harissa heat varies; taste a small amount before mixing and reduce it if preferred.

Thinly slice cabbage and grate the carrot. Toss with the remaining lime juice and one quarter of the sauce.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown tofu for 10–14 minutes, turning gently so several sides color.
Turn heat to low. Add the remaining sauce and a splash of water; stir for 1–2 minutes until hot and glossy. Serve over rice with the cold slaw. Check soy sauce for wheat.

Cook pasta according to package directions, reserving 200 ml cooking water before draining.
Combine the roasted tomatoes with cooked lentils in a wide pan. Add pasta, spinach and a little reserved water. Toss over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until spinach wilts.
Finish with lemon juice. Add enough remaining pasta water to make a loose sauce, then divide into three servings.

Grate cucumber and squeeze out excess water. Mix with yogurt, half the finely grated garlic and half the lemon juice. Refrigerate while cooking the chicken.
Slice chicken into thick strips and coat with the remaining oil, garlic, oregano and salt.
Cook chicken in a skillet over medium-high heat for 8–12 minutes, turning, until the thickest pieces reach 165°F / 74°C.

Whisk lemon juice, mustard, oil and salt in a large bowl. Stir in beans and vegetables, then fold in tuna gently.

Whisk eggs, egg whites and salt. Fold in the vegetables and crumbled feta, then pour into the dish.

Divide the cream into two bowls. Fold in half the berries and place the rest on top.

Cook shelled edamame according to its package and drain well.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Use all 8 g oil to grease a 20 cm / 8 inch square baking dish. Whisk the eggs, milk, maple syrup, baking powder, 2 g vanilla and 15 g lemon juice until combined.
Stir the oats into the egg mixture. Fold in 200 g berries and pour into the dish, distributing the fruit evenly. Scatter the remaining 100 g berries over the surface.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the center is set and reaches 160°F / 71°C. If the top browns before the middle sets, cover loosely with foil and continue baking.
Stir the yogurt with the remaining 2 g vanilla and 15 g lemon juice. Rest the oat bake for 10 minutes, then cut into four portions and serve each with one quarter of the yogurt.

recipes.name: Banana-flax cottage cheese pancakes
steps: Blend cottage cheese, eggs, milk and 120 g banana until mostly smooth. Whisk flour, flax, cinnamon and baking powder in a separate bowl, then stir in the blended mixture. Let the batter stand for 5 minutes.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Measure the oil into a small dish and use it in thin layers across the batches. For each pancake, add about 60 ml batter and spread into a small round.

Cook for 3–4 minutes until the edges look firm and bubbles hold on the surface. Flip gently and cook another 2–3 minutes. Check that the thick center reaches 160°F / 71°C and has no wet batter; reduce heat if the outside colors too quickly.
Repeat with all the batter and remaining measured oil. Slice the remaining 120 g banana. Divide the pancakes, banana and 180 g yogurt evenly into three servings.

recipes.name: Sweet potato, black bean & egg breakfast wraps
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Dice sweet potato into 1 cm cubes and peppers into small pieces. Toss with 8 g oil, cumin, paprika and 1 g salt; roast on a lined tray for 22–28 minutes, turning once, until the potato is tender.
Drain and rinse the cooked black beans. Add them to the vegetable tray for the last 5 minutes so they heat through without drying out.

Whisk eggs, whites and the remaining 1 g salt. Heat the remaining 4 g oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the egg mixture and stir gently for 5–7 minutes until set and at least 160°F / 71°C.

Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for 15–20 seconds per side. Divide all the vegetables, beans, eggs and grated cheddar evenly among four equal tortilla portions. Fold in the sides and roll tightly.

recipes.name: Thyme mushroom & ricotta egg toast
steps: Slice mushrooms and roughly chop spinach. Mix ricotta with lemon juice, thyme, 0.5 g salt and half the pepper. Toast the bread until crisp at the edges.

Heat 6 g oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook mushrooms for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their released liquid evaporates and they begin to brown. Add spinach and cook for 1 minute until wilted; transfer to a bowl.

Whisk eggs and whites with the remaining 0.5 g salt and remaining pepper. Lower the heat to medium-low, add the remaining 4 g oil and stir the eggs gently for 4–6 minutes until set and at least 160°F / 71°C.
Divide the toast between two plates. Spread each with half the ricotta mixture, then add half the mushrooms, spinach and eggs. Serve promptly so the toast stays firm.

recipes.name: Cinnamon pear quinoa porridge with walnuts
steps: Rinse quinoa in a fine sieve. Put it in a saucepan with 300 ml water and 300 ml of the measured milk. Bring just to a simmer, then cover and cook over low heat for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.

Core the pears and cut into small cubes. Put them in a second pan with 30 ml water, all the maple syrup and 2 g cinnamon. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 6–8 minutes until tender but still holding their shape.
When the quinoa is tender, stir in the remaining 150 ml milk, vanilla and remaining 1 g cinnamon. Simmer uncovered for 2–3 minutes to make a loose porridge, adding a little water if needed.
Let the porridge cool for 3 minutes, then fold in 300 g yogurt. Divide between three bowls and add the pears, their pan juices, the remaining 150 g yogurt and chopped walnuts in equal portions.

recipes.name: Miso-ginger breakfast rice with eggs & edamame
steps: Cook the dry rice according to its package water and timing. Cook the shelled edamame according to its package, then drain. Whisk miso, soy sauce, finely grated ginger and 45 ml warm water into a smooth sauce.

Slice mushrooms. Heat 8 g oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat and cook mushrooms for 6–8 minutes until browned and their liquid has evaporated. Add spinach and edamame and stir for 1–2 minutes.

Push the vegetables to one side and lower the heat to medium-low. Add the remaining 4 g oil to the empty side. Whisk eggs and whites, pour them into that space and stir gently until fully set and at least 160°F / 71°C.
Fold the cooked rice and miso sauce through the eggs and vegetables. Cook for 2–3 minutes, turning gently, until everything is hot. Divide into three bowls.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Use the measured oil to grease a 12-cup muffin pan thoroughly. Cut broccoli into very small florets and steam over simmering water for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Drain and pat dry.
Whisk eggs, whites, milk, salt and pepper in a jug. Grate the cheddar. Divide the broccoli and 75 g cheddar among the muffin cups.
Pour the egg mixture evenly into the cups, leaving a little room at the top. Scatter the remaining 25 g cheddar over them. Bake for 18–25 minutes until the centers are set and reach 160°F / 71°C.
Rest the cups for 5 minutes before easing them out with a flexible spatula. Toast the bread. Serve three egg cups and one quarter of the bread per person.

recipes.name: Apple-raisin French toast bake with yogurt
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F / 180°C. Grease a medium baking dish with all the oil. Core apples, dice them into 1 cm pieces and put in a saucepan with 40 ml water and 2 g cinnamon. Cover and soften over medium heat for 6–8 minutes.

Cut bread into 2 cm cubes. Whisk eggs, whites, milk, vanilla, maple syrup and the remaining 2 g cinnamon until combined. Fold in bread, raisins and cooked apples, including their small amount of pan liquid.
Transfer to the dish and press the bread down lightly. Let stand for 10 minutes so the custard soaks in. Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for a further 12–18 minutes until the middle reaches 160°F / 71°C and no liquid egg mixture remains. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into four portions.

steps: Rinse the buckwheat groats and put in a saucepan with 300 ml water and 300 ml soy milk. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook on low for 12–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender. Add a splash of water if needed.
Whisk soy protein into the remaining 150 ml cold soy milk until smooth. Remove the cooked buckwheat from the heat and stir in this mixture, vanilla, cinnamon and all the maple syrup.
Pit and dice peaches. Fold half into the warm buckwheat and leave for 3 minutes to soften slightly. Chop almonds coarsely.

steps: Dice onion and peppers; chop tomatoes and mince garlic. Heat 10 g oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and peppers for 7–9 minutes until softened, then add garlic, cumin, paprika and 1 g salt for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and 80 ml water. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Drain and rinse chickpeas, stir them in and simmer for another 4–5 minutes.

Whisk eggs and whites with the remaining 1 g salt. Heat the remaining 5 g oil in a separate nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the egg mixture and stir slowly for 5–7 minutes until set and at least 160°F / 71°C.
Toast the bread while the eggs cook. Divide the tomato-chickpea sauce among three shallow bowls, spoon the eggs on top and serve with equal portions of toast.

recipes.name: Chocolate-banana protein oat bake with peanut swirl
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F / 180°C and line a 20 cm / 8 inch square baking dish with baking paper. Mash 240 g banana in a large bowl. Whisk in soy milk, maple syrup, vanilla and flax; let stand for 5 minutes.
Mix oats, soy protein, cocoa and baking powder separately, breaking up any cocoa lumps. Stir the dry mixture into the banana mixture until no powdery patches remain, then spread in the lined dish.

Mix peanut butter with 20–30 ml warm water until it falls from a spoon. Dot it over the batter and drag a knife through the dots to make a shallow swirl. Slice the remaining 120 g banana and arrange on top.

Bake for 30–35 minutes until the center is firm, the edges pull slightly from the paper and a skewer comes out with moist crumbs rather than wet batter. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting into four portions.

steps: Slice mushrooms and mince garlic. Heat 8 g oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook mushrooms for 7–9 minutes until browned, then add garlic and thyme and stir for 30 seconds.

Add oats, cooked lentils, 600 ml water, 1 g salt and half the pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered over medium-low heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring frequently, until the oats soften. Add a little extra water if very thick.

Let stand for 10 minutes, then stir again to break up any chia clusters. Divide the mixture between three covered jars and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until the seeds swell and the oats soften.
Dice the peeled mango. Keep half for topping and mash the other half with a fork into a chunky puree. Refrigerate both in covered containers while the pots set.

Heat 8 g oil in a wide nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add sweet potato and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned at the edges. Transfer to a plate.

Add the remaining 4 g oil, onion and peppers to the skillet. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add tempeh, cumin, paprika, salt and 60 ml water. Cover and cook for 6–8 minutes, or longer if the tempeh package requires it.
Return sweet potato to the pan with the cooked, drained corn. Stir over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until hot throughout and most of the liquid evaporates.

Dice the remaining zucchini, carrot and onion. Heat oil in a wide pot over medium heat and soften onion and carrot for 7–9 minutes. Add minced garlic and the remaining oregano; stir for 30 seconds.

Add chopped tomatoes, the remaining salt, pepper and 900 ml water. Bring to a gentle simmer, add the meatballs without stacking, cover and simmer for 12–16 minutes until their centers reach 165°F / 74°C.

Cook soba according to its package, adding edamame only for the cooking time specified on the edamame package. Drain, rinse briefly with cold water and drain thoroughly.
Whisk soy sauce, lime juice, grated ginger, maple syrup and 20 ml water in a large bowl. Shred cabbage, cut carrot into fine matchsticks and thinly slice cucumber.
Toast sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring continuously until lightly golden. Immediately tip onto a cool plate to prevent scorching.

Shred cabbage and carrot. Whisk yogurt, half the lemon juice, half the mustard, chopped dill and half the salt; toss with the vegetables and refrigerate.

Dice tomato, cucumber and remaining onion. Toss with half the lemon juice, one third of the oil and the remaining parsley and salt. Keep chilled while the beef cooks.
Mix yogurt with the remaining lemon juice and 15 ml water. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat with the remaining oil; add kofta in one layer without crowding.

While pork rests, heat another third of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook sliced mushrooms for 7–9 minutes until their water evaporates; add minced garlic and remaining thyme for the final minute.

Pat peeled shrimp dry. Dice pineapple, carrot and onion, and mince ginger and garlic. Beat eggs in a small bowl; keep the raw shrimp and egg utensils away from the cooked rice.

Add the remaining oil, onion and carrot; stir-fry for 5–7 minutes. Stir in garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, push vegetables aside, and add eggs. Scramble until fully set, then mix with the vegetables.

Add remaining oil and diced onion to the skillet. Cook over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, then stir in minced garlic, oregano, salt and pepper for 30 seconds. Add chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.

Stir spinach into the tomato sauce until wilted. Fold in pasta, cooked chicken, chopped basil and enough reserved water to make a loose sauce. Transfer to a baking dish and dot ricotta evenly over the top.

Cook rice according to its package. Drain cooked lentils well. Finely dice onion and chop tomatoes, keeping half the tomatoes separate for the baking dish.

Heat remaining oil in a skillet over medium heat and soften onion for 6 minutes. Add turkey, minced garlic, oregano, paprika and salt; break up and cook for 8–10 minutes until turkey reaches 165°F / 74°C.

Add tomatoes, chickpeas, salt and 200 ml water. Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 10–12 minutes until the tomatoes break down and the sauce thickens slightly.

Add vegetables and 50 ml water to the skillet. Cover for 3 minutes, uncover and stir-fry for 4–5 minutes until just tender. Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds.

Heat remaining oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook patties for approximately 5–7 minutes per side, turning once carefully, until each center reaches 160°F / 71°C; lower heat if they brown too quickly.

Place salmon on a second lined tray, rub with remaining oil and half the salt, and bake for 12–18 minutes until the thickest part reaches 145°F / 63°C. Remove any bones and flake with a clean fork.

steps: Cut tenderloin across the grain into strips about 1 cm thick. Toss with half the oil, minced garlic, cumin, paprika and half the salt. Slice peppers and onion into similar-width strips.
Mash avocado with half the lime juice and 15–30 ml water to make a spoonable cream. Stir in chopped cilantro and the remaining salt. Drain and rinse cooked black beans.

Add remaining oil and the mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 6–8 minutes until browned, then add onion and carrot and cook another 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, thyme, pepper and tomato paste for 1 minute.

Return beef and add barley, tomatoes, salt and the water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a gentle simmer, cover loosely and cook for 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until barley is tender. Add small amounts of water if it becomes dry.

Trim and pat dry the pork. Mix half the mustard with one quarter of the oil, minced garlic, pepper and the remaining thyme; rub over the tenderloin.

Heat oil in a wide lidded saucepan over medium heat. Cook onion for 6–8 minutes, then stir in ginger, garlic and curry powder for 45 seconds until fragrant.
Add coconut milk, 250 ml water, salt and cauliflower. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 8–10 minutes until the cauliflower is nearly tender.

Cook pasta according to its package, reserving 250 ml cooking water before draining. Pat peeled shrimp dry while the pasta cooks.

Bake fish for approximately 12–18 minutes, checking early for thin pieces, until the thickest strips reach 145°F / 63°C. Remove finished pieces to a clean warm plate.
Meanwhile shred cabbage and grate carrot. Drain cooked corn and toss with cabbage, carrot, half the lime juice, chopped cilantro and remaining salt.

Mash avocado with yogurt and remaining lime juice until mostly smooth. Add 15–30 ml water if needed for a spreadable sauce. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20–30 seconds on each side.

Use one third of the measured oil to lightly coat a lined baking tray. Shape the mixture into a low loaf roughly 8 cm thick. Mix tomato paste, mustard and 40 ml water; spread over the loaf.

Heat one third of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add spinach and stir for 1–2 minutes until wilted; cool slightly, squeeze out excess liquid and chop. Mix with ricotta, half the minced garlic, pepper and half the salt.

Divide the ricotta mixture across the chicken cutlets, leaving a small border. Roll each from a short end and secure with a toothpick; keep raw chicken away from the cooked quinoa and remaining vegetables.

Place chopped tomatoes in a baking dish with remaining garlic, oil, salt and oregano. Set chicken rolls seam-side down in the tomatoes and bake for 25–35 minutes until the center of every roll, including its filling, reaches 165°F / 74°C.

Cook soba in water according to its package, reserving 150 ml cooking water. Drain and rinse briefly to stop sticking. Toast sesame in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 2 minutes and set aside.

Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Cut broccoli into small florets and carrots into thin half-moons. Toss with half the oil and half the salt; roast on a lined tray for 20–25 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned at the edges.

Finely dice the onion and garlic. Cook in half the oil over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in paprika and cumin for the final 30 seconds, then take off the heat.

Form six firm patties and brush both sides with the remaining oil. Bake on a lined tray for 25–30 minutes, turning carefully after 18 minutes, until the edges are browned and the centers are hot and firm.

Mash the chickpeas and half the edamame coarsely with a fork. Stir in the remaining edamame, cumin and half the salt; keep some whole beans for texture.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice, finely grated garlic, remaining salt and 45–60 ml water. It will thicken at first; keep whisking until smooth and spreadable.
Grate the carrot, dice cucumber and shred romaine. Pat the cucumber dry. Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry skillet, about 20 seconds per side, so they bend without cracking.

Roast chickpeas for 25–30 minutes, shaking twice, until their surfaces are dry and lightly crisp. They will soften once added to soup, so keep them separate until serving.

Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, finely grated ginger, maple syrup and 50–70 ml warm water until smooth and pourable.

Place pepper halves cut-side up in a baking dish with 60 ml water. Cover tightly and bake for 15 minutes to begin softening them.
Drain tofu and press dry with a clean towel. Crumble it coarsely. Dice onion and tomatoes; mince garlic. Heat oil in a skillet and cook onion over medium heat for 6 minutes.
Add tofu, garlic, cumin, paprika and salt. Cook for 7–9 minutes, stirring, until hot and lightly browned. Stir in tomatoes and drained cooked corn for 3 minutes, then fold in quinoa and lime juice.

Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and beginning to pop. Tip onto a plate and cool.

Rinse and drain the cooked black beans. Put in a saucepan with minced garlic, remaining cumin and salt, and 80 ml water. Simmer for 6–8 minutes; mash about one third of the beans to thicken, then add half the lime juice.
Shred romaine and dice tomatoes. Warm tortillas in a dry skillet for 20–30 seconds per side until flexible. Keep them covered with a clean towel.

steps: Rinse the dry red lentils thoroughly. Dice onion, finely chop ginger and garlic, and cut cauliflower into small florets. Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.

Trim green beans and steam for 5–7 minutes until tender-crisp. Cool briefly under running water and drain well. Finely dice the onion and chop dill.

Drain tofu, press dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook tofu for 10–12 minutes, turning gently, until the edges are golden and the centers are hot.
Whisk tahini, mustard, lemon juice, grated garlic, salt and 60–80 ml water into a smooth dressing. Stir in dill and onion.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Cook buckwheat according to its package. Carefully loosen six to nine large cabbage leaves from the head; blanch them in simmering water for 3–5 minutes until flexible, then drain. Thin the thick central ribs with a knife.

Finely chop mushrooms and onion. Cook them in half the oil over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes until the mushrooms have released their liquid and it has evaporated. Add half the minced garlic and half the thyme for 1 minute.

Mix the mushroom mixture with drained cooked lentils, buckwheat and half the salt. Mash a small amount of the filling so it holds together. Divide among the cabbage leaves, fold in the sides and roll into parcels.

In the same pan, warm remaining oil with remaining garlic for 30 seconds. Add chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, remaining thyme and salt, and 200 ml water. Simmer for 10 minutes, crushing the tomatoes to make a loose sauce.

Spread half the sauce in a baking dish, arrange rolls seam-side down and spoon over remaining sauce. Cover and bake for 35–40 minutes until the cabbage is tender and filling is hot throughout. Divide rolls and sauce into three portions.

recipes.name: Roasted zucchini & basil-tofu pasta salad
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Drain tofu and pat dry, then cut into 2 cm cubes. Cut zucchini into thick half-moons. Toss both with oil and half the salt and spread on a lined tray.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, turning halfway, until tofu edges brown and zucchini is tender. Let cool for 10 minutes while preparing the pasta.
Cook pasta according to its package until tender. Drain, rinse briefly with cool water and drain thoroughly; excess water will dilute the dressing.
Finely chop basil and garlic. Whisk with balsamic vinegar, lemon juice, remaining salt and 30 ml water. Dice tomatoes and stir them into the dressing so their juices join the sauce.
Fold pasta, roasted tofu and zucchini into the tomato-basil mixture. Rest for 5 minutes, toss again and divide into three portions. Refrigerate promptly if serving later.

recipes.name: Broccoli-cheddar baked potatoes with cottage-cheese cream
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Scrub three similar-size potatoes totaling the measured weight, dry them and prick each several times with a fork. Rub with half the oil and half the salt.
Bake directly on a tray for 50–65 minutes until the centers are soft when pierced; larger potatoes may need longer. Meanwhile, dice onion and cut broccoli into small florets.
Heat remaining oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook onion for 6–8 minutes. Add broccoli and 60 ml water, cover and steam for 5–7 minutes until tender. Uncover and evaporate remaining water.
Blend or mash cottage cheese with mustard, pepper and remaining salt. Grate the cheddar, choosing a cheese labeled suitable for vegetarians.

Split each hot potato and loosen the flesh with a fork. Add cottage-cheese cream and broccoli, sprinkle with cheddar and return to the oven for 4–6 minutes until the cheese melts. Serve one filled potato per portion.

recipes.name: Spinach, ricotta & white-bean folded tortilla melts
steps: Rinse and drain cooked white beans, then mash coarsely. Dice tomatoes finely, letting excess juice drain into a small bowl. Mince garlic and grate mozzarella; use cheeses labeled suitable for vegetarians.
Heat half the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add garlic for 30 seconds, then spinach and oregano. Cook for 2–3 minutes until wilted and most moisture has evaporated.

Mix beans, ricotta, cooked spinach, salt and half the mozzarella. Spread the filling over one half of each tortilla, keeping a 2 cm border. Scatter over remaining mozzarella and fold the tortillas shut.

Brush the skillet with remaining oil and cook the folded tortillas in batches over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until crisp and the centers are piping hot. Lower the heat if the bread browns before the filling warms.

Rest for 2 minutes before cutting so the filling settles. Divide into three portions and serve with diced tomatoes. Keep the drained tomato juice for another use or stir a little into the tomatoes for serving.

recipes.name: Slow-simmered tempeh & mushroom pasta ragu
steps: Finely dice onion and carrot, chop mushrooms and mince garlic. Crumble tempeh into small pieces. Heat oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat.

Cook onion and carrot for 8–10 minutes until softened. Add mushrooms and tempeh, increase to medium-high and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until mushrooms lose their moisture and tempeh begins to brown.

Stir in garlic, tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute. Add chopped tomatoes, salt and 250 ml water. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick; follow any longer tempeh package requirement.
Cook pasta according to its package. Reserve 150 ml cooking water before draining. Tear the basil leaves into small pieces.
Fold pasta and basil into the ragu. Add reserved pasta water a little at a time until the sauce coats the noodles, and heat for 2 minutes. Divide into three portions.

recipes.name: Lentil, pea & thyme shepherd’s pie
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Peel potatoes if desired, cut into equal chunks and simmer in water for 15–20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly and steam-dry for 2 minutes.
Dice onion and carrot and mince garlic. Heat two thirds of the oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat and cook onion and carrot for 8–10 minutes. Add garlic, thyme and tomato paste for 1 minute.

Add drained cooked lentils, peas, half the salt and 200 ml water. Simmer for 10–12 minutes until carrots and peas are tender, following the peas’ package cooking instructions. Mash a few lentils to make a thick filling.

Warm the soy milk without boiling. Mash potatoes with it, remaining oil and remaining salt until smooth enough to spread. Spoon lentil filling into a baking dish and cover with the mash, roughing the surface with a fork.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the edges bubble and the top begins to brown. Rest for 10 minutes before dividing into four portions; the filling will firm slightly as it stands.

Cook rice with the water amount and timing on its package. Keep covered off the heat for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Dice onion and finely chop ginger and garlic. Heat remaining oil in a deep saucepan over medium heat and cook onion for 7–8 minutes. Add ginger, garlic and curry powder and stir for 1 minute.

Add coconut milk, rinsed cooked chickpeas, remaining salt and 150 ml water. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Fold in roasted tofu and cauliflower and simmer for 5 minutes more until everything is piping hot.
Stir in lime juice and loosen with a little water if the sauce is too thick. Divide curry and rice into three portions, keeping the rice separate for storage if convenient.

recipes.name: Smoky seitan & black-bean fajita tray with rice

Toss peppers and onion with two thirds of the spice mixture. Spread in a large roasting dish and roast for 15 minutes until beginning to soften.
Cook rice according to its package. Rest covered for 5 minutes before fluffing. Rinse and drain cooked black beans.

Toss seitan with the remaining spice mixture and add to the roasting dish with black beans and 50 ml water. Stir and roast for another 12–15 minutes until vegetables are tender and seitan and beans are piping hot.
Stir remaining lime juice, remaining salt and chopped cilantro into the rice. Divide rice and the roasted mixture into three portions, spooning the pan juices over the top.

recipes.name: Sesame tofu, green-bean & mushroom noodle skillet
steps: Drain tofu and press dry, then cut into 2 cm cubes. Trim green beans and cut into short lengths; slice mushrooms. Cook soba according to its package, drain and rinse briefly to prevent sticking.
Toast sesame seeds in a dry wide skillet over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Remove to a small bowl. Whisk soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice and 80 ml water.
Heat two thirds of the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Brown tofu in a single layer for 10–12 minutes, turning gently, then transfer to a plate.

Add remaining oil, mushrooms and beans. Cook for 4 minutes, then add finely chopped ginger and garlic, the soy mixture and another 50 ml water. Cover and simmer for 5–7 minutes until the beans are tender-crisp.

Return tofu, add noodles and half the sesame seeds, and toss over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until hot and coated. Add water sparingly if the pan dries out. Divide into three portions and finish with remaining seeds.

recipes.name: Kidney-bean & quinoa zucchini boats with pumpkin seeds
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the soft centers, leaving walls about 1 cm thick. Chop the scooped flesh and set aside. Place shells in a baking dish with 60 ml water, cover and bake for 15 minutes.
Rinse quinoa and cook according to its package, then rest covered for 5 minutes. Use ready-cooked canned kidney beans only; rinse and drain them. This timing is not suitable for dry kidney beans.

Dice onion and tomatoes and mince garlic. Heat oil in a skillet and cook onion over medium heat for 7 minutes. Add chopped zucchini flesh, garlic, cumin and oregano; cook for 5 minutes until most liquid evaporates.

Stir in tomatoes, kidney beans and salt and simmer for 8–10 minutes. Mash a few beans, then fold in cooked quinoa. Spoon generously into the softened zucchini shells, placing extra filling around them.
Scatter pumpkin seeds over the filling. Bake uncovered for 20–25 minutes until zucchini is tender and filling is hot throughout; cover loosely if seeds brown too quickly. Divide into three portions.

recipes.name: Smoky chickpea-cabbage braise with crisp tofu & couscous
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Drain tofu, pat dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Toss with half the oil, half the paprika and one third of the salt. Roast on a lined tray for 25–30 minutes, turning once, until golden at the edges.
Thinly slice onion and cabbage, cut carrots into small half-moons and chop tomatoes. Heat remaining oil in a large lidded pan over medium heat and cook onion and carrots for 7–8 minutes.

Add minced garlic and remaining paprika for 30 seconds. Fold in cabbage, tomatoes, rinsed cooked chickpeas, remaining salt and 200 ml water. Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cabbage and carrots are tender.
Prepare couscous with the boiling-water quantity and standing time on its package. Fluff with a fork, then stir in half the lemon juice.

recipes.name: Red-lentil spinach dal with edamame & rice
steps: Rinse the dry red lentils thoroughly. Dice onion and tomatoes, and finely chop ginger and garlic. Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook onion for 8–10 minutes until soft.
Stir in ginger, garlic, turmeric and cumin for 1 minute. Add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until beginning to collapse. Add lentils, coconut milk, salt and 900 ml water and bring to a boil.

Lower to a gentle simmer and cook for at least 30 minutes, stirring frequently and adding water if needed to prevent sticking. The lentils should be completely soft and breaking down. Simmer longer if any remain firm.

Meanwhile cook rice according to its package and rest covered for 5 minutes. Add shelled edamame to the dal near the end and simmer for at least its full package cooking time, extending the cooking as required.

recipes.name: White-bean, mushroom & pea barley pot
steps: Rinse barley, slice mushrooms, dice onion and mince garlic. Heat half the oil in a large heavy saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook mushrooms for 8–10 minutes until their released liquid evaporates and the edges brown, then remove to a bowl.
Add remaining oil and onion to the pan. Cook over medium heat for 7 minutes, then add garlic and thyme for 1 minute. Stir in barley to coat it.

Add salt and 1 litre water, bring to a boil and simmer gently for 30–40 minutes, or the barley package time, stirring occasionally. Add more water in small amounts if the barley begins to stick before becoming tender.
Rinse and drain cooked white beans. Return mushrooms to the pot with beans and peas. Simmer for 7–10 minutes until hot and the peas are cooked, following any longer pea package cooking time.
Fold in spinach for 2–3 minutes until wilted, then stir in lemon juice. The finished dish should be loose and spoonable rather than dry; add water if necessary. Divide into four portions.

steps: Cook rice according to its package. Cut broccoli into small florets and steam for 6–8 minutes until tender-crisp. Chop pineapple and peppers into bite-size pieces.

Cut tempeh into cubes. Simmer in a wide skillet with 80 ml water, covered, for 5 minutes. Uncover, evaporate the water and add two thirds of the oil. Brown tempeh for 7–9 minutes, turning, then transfer to a plate; follow any longer package cooking requirement.
Whisk tomato paste, vinegar, soy sauce, maple syrup and 100 ml water until smooth. Finely chop ginger and garlic.

Heat remaining oil in the skillet. Cook peppers over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes, add pineapple and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in ginger and garlic for 30 seconds. Add the sauce and simmer for 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened.

Return tempeh and toss for 2–3 minutes until hot and glossy, adding a little water if the sauce reduces too far. Fold broccoli into the rice and divide between three portions with the pineapple tempeh.

recipes.name: Sweet-potato black-bean cakes with quinoa & lime salad
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Cut sweet potato into 2 cm cubes and steam for 12–15 minutes until very soft. Drain thoroughly and spread out for 5 minutes so excess moisture can escape. Cook rinsed quinoa according to its package.

Rinse and drain cooked black beans, pat dry and mash coarsely with the sweet potato. Pulse oats into coarse crumbs, or crush with a rolling pin. Stir into the mash with grated garlic, cumin, paprika and half the salt; rest for 10 minutes.

Form eight firm cakes. Brush a lined tray and the tops of the cakes with the measured oil. Bake for 30–35 minutes, turning carefully after 20 minutes, until firm with browned edges. Let stand for 5 minutes before moving.
Toast pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Chop romaine and tomatoes. Stir half the lime juice and remaining salt into the cooked quinoa.

Divide quinoa, romaine and tomatoes into four portions. Add two cakes per serving, scatter over pumpkin seeds and finish with remaining lime juice. Keep raw salad separate from hot cakes when packing.

recipes.name: Harissa seitan, chickpea & vegetable roast with couscous
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Cut carrots into thin batons and zucchini into thick half-moons. Slice ready-cooked seitan into strips, and rinse and drain cooked chickpeas.
Mix harissa, oil, minced garlic, half the lemon juice and salt. Toss carrots with one third of the mixture and roast in a large dish for 12 minutes; carrots need a head start to soften.

Toss zucchini, chickpeas and seitan with remaining harissa mixture. Add them to the carrots, spread evenly and roast for 20–25 minutes more, stirring once, until carrots are tender and seitan and beans are piping hot. Add 30 ml water if the paste begins to scorch.
Prepare couscous with the water amount and standing time on its package. Fluff and mix with remaining lemon juice and finely chopped parsley.
Divide couscous and roasted mixture into three portions, spooning over pan juices. Harissa heat and salt vary; use a mild product if preferred and check its ingredient label for personal exclusions.

recipes.name: Spinach-ricotta lentil lasagna bake
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Use whole-wheat pasta in a short shape such as penne. Cook for 2 minutes less than its package time because it will finish in the oven. Drain, reserving 150 ml cooking water.

Dice onion and tomatoes and mince garlic. Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook onion for 7–8 minutes. Add garlic and oregano for 1 minute, then tomatoes and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until saucy.
Rinse and drain cooked lentils and stir them into the tomato sauce. Put spinach in a separate pan with 30 ml water, cover and wilt for 2–3 minutes. Cool briefly, squeeze out excess liquid and chop.

Mix spinach with ricotta, choosing ricotta and mozzarella labeled suitable for vegetarians. Fold pasta into the lentil sauce, adding enough reserved cooking water to keep it loose. Layer half in a baking dish, spoon over half the spinach ricotta and repeat; top with grated mozzarella.
Cover and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover for 10–15 minutes until bubbling and lightly golden. Rest for 10 minutes before dividing into four portions.

recipes.name: Chickpea-feta shakshuka with whole-grain toast
steps: Dice onion, peppers and tomatoes and mince garlic. Heat oil in a large lidded skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and peppers for 10–12 minutes until soft, stirring occasionally.
Stir in garlic, paprika and cumin for 1 minute. Add tomatoes, salt and 100 ml water and simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes, crushing tomatoes with a spoon, until a thick sauce forms.
Rinse and drain cooked chickpeas and stir them into the sauce. Simmer for 3–4 minutes until hot. Beat whole eggs and egg whites together in a bowl, using the measured edible weights.

Make shallow spaces in the sauce and pour the egg mixture into them in portions. Crumble vegetarian-suitable feta over the top. Cover and cook over low heat for 7–12 minutes until eggs are fully set and reach 160°F / 71°C in the center; avoid leaving runny pockets.
Toast the bread while the eggs cook. Divide shakshuka and toast into four portions and serve promptly. For reheating, keep toast separate and heat the cooked egg dish thoroughly.
